title: NRI Selling Joint Property: Capital Gains Tax Explained

faq.q: What is the TDS rate for an NRI selling property?
faq.a: For NRIs, the TDS rate on long-term capital gains from property sale is typically 20% (plus surcharge and cess). For short-term capital gains, it's 30% (plus surcharge and cess).

faq.q: Can an NRI claim capital gains exemptions like Section 54 or 54EC?
faq.a: Yes, an NRI can claim exemptions under sections like 54 (reinvestment in residential property) or 54EC (investment in specified bonds) on their share of capital gains, provided they meet all the stipulated conditions.

faq.q: How is capital gain calculated for jointly owned property?
faq.a: Each co-owner calculates capital gain based on their proportionate share of the sale consideration, after deducting their share of the indexed cost of acquisition and improvement.

faq.q: What documents are needed for an NRI to repatriate funds from property sale?
faq.a: An NRI typically needs a certificate from a Chartered Accountant in Form 15CB and must submit Form 15CA to the authorised dealer bank for repatriation of funds.

faq.q: Does the resident co-owner also face higher TDS if one co-owner is an NRI?
faq.a: No, the TDS provisions apply individually. The resident co-owner will be subject to TDS rules applicable to residents (1% if sale consideration exceeds ₹50 lakhs), while the NRI co-owner faces the higher NRI-specific TDS rates on their share.

faq.q: Can an NRI claim indexation benefit on long-term capital gains?
faq.a: Yes, NRIs are eligible for the indexation benefit to adjust the cost of acquisition for inflation when calculating long-term capital gains from property sales.
